281:
Pursuant to the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 3-3-20, the sale of malt beverages and/or wine shall be permitted on election days as the same are defined in the Official Code of Georgia Annotated; provided, however, that it shall nonetheless be unlawful for any person to sell malt beverages and wine within 250 feet of any polling place or of the outer edge of any building within which such polling place is established on primary or election days.
(Code 1969, § 3-32; Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03)
State Law reference— Sales of alcoholic beverages on Sundays, election days and Christmas Day, O.C.G.A. § 3-3-20.
282:
It shall be unlawful for any licensee under this chapter to encourage or permit the consumption of any alcoholic beverages on the premises for which the permit was issued at any time other than the permitted hours of operation as set forth in sections 6-132 and 6-319 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 20-2001, § 1, 9-17-01; Ord. No. 10, 2003, § 4, 9-15-03; Ord. No. 2-2004, § 2, 2-9-04)
283:
(a) A special location permit and license for a restaurant or eating establishment as defined in section 6-102, shall be required for each place of business when an applicant applies for the right to sell wine and malt beverages in a portion of the C-1 downtown business district. All such applicants shall file their application on forms generally required by this Code, and otherwise meet all other requirements of holding all licenses granted by the city.
(b) With regard to any license within the downtown business district, which might be granted by the city commission under this section, the following rules and regulations shall apply to such license holder in addition to all other regulations and requirements of the city, or any state, or federal governing authority regarding such license holders:
(1) No screen, partition, tinted windows, or other device which prevents a clear view into the interior of the retail outlet from the street, nor any booth within, shall be permitted. No advertising of prices or signs outside the restaurant, nor any "beer and/or wine for sale" or other similar alcoholic beverage descriptive sign shall be allowed to be placed either in front of the building of the eating establishment, or on any windows open for view of the public.
(2) Upon the transfer of the premises, closing of the establishment, or death of the license holder, no transfer of the license from the approved license holder shall be permitted without prior approval of the city.
(3) The license holder shall maintain, in proper order at all times, all books and records with regard to the sale of food within the eating establishment in proportion to the sale of wine and/or malt beverages, to be certain that the establishment derives no more than 60 percent of its gross revenues from the sale of wine and malt beverages. These records may be reviewed by the city manager, or his designee, at all times during normal business hours of the license holder. Furthermore, not less than annually at the time of renewal, the license holder shall certify, through a certified public accountant or other person capable of providing the certificate, that a thorough review of the books and records of the license holder has been conducted, and that the licensee is in compliance with the restriction of 60 percent sales as set forth in the requirements of this Code.
(4) The commission shall have the right to promulgate any and all other reasonable regulations that might govern any individual eating establishments, their configuration, or requirements for continuation of a license, as might be required within the downtown business district, this section, or otherwise to comply with the intention of the commission in relation thereto.
(c) Any license granted hereunder shall have affixed thereto a special location permit, which shows that the license is granted and complies with the zoning restrictions on the location of malt beverages and wine restaurant consumption licenses for the specific defined and specially zoned location, as set forth in section 94-116.1 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 1-2003, § 6, 3-10-03; Ord. No. 8,2010, § 3, 6-14-10)
284:
(a) A license, to be granted hereunder, for retail on-premises consumption of malt beverages may be granted in areas of the city properly zoned for an on-premises consumption establishment, and not otherwise prohibited by the prohibited location restriction of section 6-131 of this Code. No retail consumption licensee shall keep any beer or wine, or other alcoholic beverages, in any place except the licensed place of business. No retail consumption licensee shall be permitted to enter into any type of arrangements whereby distilled spirits ordered by the licensee or stored by a licensed wholesaler, or otherwise, are kept on the premises at any time.
(b) It is prohibited for customers to leave the premises with open containers of alcoholic beverages. It is the licensee's responsibility to insure that no such open containers are carried out of the premises. Further, customers shall not gather outside of an establishment which allows consumption on the premises and consume alcoholic beverages. It is prohibited for the manager, or any employee, to allow such persons to gather outside and consume alcoholic beverages.
(c) No retail consumption licensee shall permit, encourage or induce any employee or agent to solicit the purchase by a patron of any drink, whether alcoholic or nonalcoholic; or try to solicit money to insure that patrons must participate in the consumption of such beverages through promotions, discounts, or contests. Further, no licensee shall pay a commission or other compensation based solely on the frequency in which a patron purchases beverages while on the premises.
(d) No retail consumption licensee shall permit excessive noise that can create a breach of the peace, a disturbance, or otherwise may be distinctly heard beyond the physical boundaries of the property upon which the license is granted.
(e) No patron of any establishment which allows on-the-premises consumption under a proper license from the city shall be permitted to bring any form of wine, beer, liquor or other alcoholic beverage, onto the premises in any cooler, container, or other carrying device. Thus, the practice of "brown bagging" or "bring your own bottle" (BYOB) shall, under no circumstances, be allowed within the corporate limits of the city.
(f) The chief of police, or his designee, may immediately close an establishment licensed under this chapter in case of emergency, for safety of the public, or to investigate a crime. The period of closure shall not exceed 72 hours without the right for an emergency hearing before the municipal court concerning the circumstances surrounding the emergency closure, and reasons for its continuation, or termination of closure.
(Ord. No. 1-2003, § 6, 3-10-03)
285:
(a) The downtown entertainment district, which is defined as:
The area bordered by Ware Street, Knight's Alley Road, Sterling Holloway Place, Grace Street, Warehouse Street, Sterling Holloway Place, and Prior Street, and as shown on the certain map labeled "Entertainment District Cedartown, Georgia." A copy of said map will be kept and available for review in the offices of the city clerk and downtown development authority. For the purposes of this definition, any licensed establishment on property that abuts the described boundaries shall be considered to be located within the downtown entertainment district.
(b) Open container/off-premises consumption of alcoholic beverages in the downtown entertainment district shall be allowed only in compliance with the following regulations:
(1) Type of container. Any establishment within the downtown entertainment district licensed to dispense alcoholic beverages by the drink for consumption on the premises is authorized to dispense an alcoholic beverage in a plastic or aluminum cup conforming to cup specifications promulgated by the Cedartown Downtown Development Authority for removal from the premises.
(2) Size limited to a maximum of 16 oz. No container in which an alcoholic beverage is dispensed and removed from the licensed premises shall exceed 16 fluid ounces in size. No person shall hold in possession on the streets and sidewalks, in parks and squares, or in other public places within the downtown entertainment district area any open alcoholic beverage container which exceeds 16 fluid ounces in size.
(3) Drinking from unapproved can, bottle, or glass prohibited. Within the downtown entertainment district, it shall be unlawful for any person to drink or attempt to drink any alcoholic beverage from a can, bottle, or glass or to possess in an open can, bottle, or glass any alcoholic beverage on the streets, sidewalks, right-of-way, and parking lots, whether public or private. This prohibition shall not apply to cups conforming to the specifications promulgated by the Cedartown Downtown Development Authority as described in this Code section.
(4) Hours of public consumption of alcoholic beverages permitted within the downtown entertainment district. Alcoholic beverages purchased within the downtown entertainment district pursuant to this provision may be consumed within the downtown entertainment district on the streets, sidewalks, rights-of-way, and parking lots, whether public or private (except as otherwise exempted in this Code section), during the hours of 5:00 p.m. to 11:00 p.m. on Thursdays and Fridays, and 11:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. on Saturdays and Sundays, unless otherwise prohibited by law.
(5) Signage. Any establishment that allows patrons to leave an establishment with an alcoholic beverage as regulated herein shall have an 11-inch by 17-inch sign posted at the doors within public view so that patrons exiting the establishment can read the following:
"All patrons leaving this establishment with an alcoholic beverage do hereby take full responsibility to only consume an alcoholic beverage in the immediate entertainment district and any individual that leaves the permitted area with an alcoholic beverage is in violation of City Code and may be subject to a citation and/or fine, and/or arrest, and/or incarceration." The downtown development authority will design and make the standardized signage available to all licensed establishments within the downtown entertainment district.
(6) Alcohol ratio. This section does not alter the ratio requirements of licensed establishments within the downtown entertainment district.
(Ord. No. 9-2024, § 1, 9-9-24)
287:
(a) It shall be unlawful to grant a license for the sale of malt beverages and/or wine within the following areas in the city:
(1) Any residential zoning district.
(2) A measured distance of 300 feet of any girl's club, boy's club, YMCA, community center, Salvation Army Center, public park or other public playground or recreational facility owned or operated by the city.
(3) A measured distance of 300 feet of any alcoholic treatment center owned or operated by the state or any local governing authority.
(4) A measured distance of 300 feet of any church, school ground, or college campus.
(5) No malt beverage and/or wine sales shall be permitted within the defined area of the C-1 central business district except as described in the Downtown Development Authority Act (section 2-96 of the Code). Restaurants in that area only (not the remainder of C-1) may sell beer and wine as a part of an eating establishment pursuant to section 6-102 of the Code.
(6) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Code section or elsewhere in the City's Code of Ordinances contrary, the distance limitations described in subsections (a)(l-4) hereof shall not apply to the retail sale of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises where such retailer has complied with the other applicable provisions of the City's Code of Ordinances and state laws related to the same.
(b) It shall be unlawful to grant a license for the sale of distilled spirits within 300 feet of any church building or within 600 feet of any school building, educational building, school grounds, or college campus within the city limits.
(c) "Measured" for purposes of this section, shall mean measured in accordance with the statues, rules, and regulations of the State of Georgia or the Georgia Department of Revenue, as such may be amended from time to time.
(Code 1969, § 3-23; Ord. No. 1-2003, §§ 3, 4, 3-10-03; Ord. No. 9,2006, § 1, 9-11-06; Ord. No. 4-2012, § 1, 4-9-21)
288:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to sell, give away, offer for sale, or in any manner disperse or deliver, any malt beverages and/or wine by the package within the corporate limits of the city between the hours of 12:00 a.m. (midnight) until 12:30 p.m. on each and every Sunday; and from 11:30 p.m. on each and every Sunday until 8:00 a.m. on each and every Monday; and from 12:00 a.m. midnight Christmas Eve until 8:00 a.m. on the day following Christmas of each year.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to sell, give away, offer for sale, or in any manner disperse or deliver any malt beverages and/or wine by the drink within the corporate limits of the city between the hours of 1:30 a.m. until 8:00 a.m. each and every Monday through Saturday; and from 1:30 a.m. until 11:00 a.m. on each and every Sunday; and from 11:30 p.m. on each and every Sunday, until 8:00 a.m. on each and every Monday; and from 12:00 a.m. midnight on Christmas Eve until 8:00 a.m. on the day following Christmas each year.
(Ord. No. 2-2012, § 1, 3-12-12; Ord. No. 5-2021, § 2, 12-13-21; Ord. No. 3-2025, § 2, 3-10-25)

290:
(a) Unless the context demands otherwise, the words and terms used in this article shall have the same definitions and meanings as stated in the applicable provisions of title 3 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated and section 6-1.
(b) The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Business location or outlet means the location or proposed location of a retail malt beverage or wine outlet.
(Code 1969, § 3-40; Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03)
Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.
291:
It shall be unlawful to sell, store or offer to sell malt beverages and/or wine at wholesale or retail within the corporate limits of the city without having the appropriate license for such sale, or to carry on such activity in violation of the terms of such license or this chapter.
(Code 1969, § 3-41; Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03)
292:
(a) A separate license shall be required for each malt beverages and/or wine outlet, and separate application shall be made for each outlet.
(b) Licenses under this section shall be nontransferable.
(c) Immediately upon the sale or closing of an outlet, it shall be the duty of the licensee to surrender his license to the commission.
(Code 1969, § 3-42; Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03)
293:
(a) Licenses under this article shall be classified as follows:
(1) Retail malt beverages and/or wine package. The retail malt beverages and/or wine package license shall permit only the sale of malt beverages and/or wine in packages at retail.
(2) Retail sales of wine for consumption on the premises. The license for retail sales of malt beverages and/or wine for consumption on the premises shall permit the sale of wine by the bottle or by the glass for consumption on the premises.
(3) Wholesale. The wholesale malt beverages and/or wine distributor license shall permit only the sale of wine at wholesale.
(4) Brewery. The brewery license shall permit the manufacture or brewing of malt beverages.
(5) Brewpub. The license for a brewpub allows for an eating establishment to sell beer or malt beverages that are manufactured or brewed at the establishment.
(6) Winery. The license for a winery allows for the manufacture of wine.
(b) The following license fees shall be paid to the city clerk of the city prior to the issuance or renewal of any malt beverages and/or wine license:
(1) Retail malt beverages and/or wine package. The license fee for operation of a malt beverages and/or wine retail package license for one calendar year or any part thereof shall be as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges. No license fee shall be refunded.
(2) Retail sales of malt beverages and/or wine for consumption on the premises. The license fee for retail sales of malt beverages and/or wine for consumption on the premises for one calendar year or any part thereof shall be as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges. No license fee shall be refunded.
(3) Malt beverages and/or wine wholesale distributor. The license fee for operation of a wholesale distributor for one calendar year or any part thereof shall be as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges. No license fee shall be refunded.
(4) Brewery. The license fee for operation of a brewery for one calendar year or any part thereof shall be as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges. No license fee shall be refunded.
(5) Brewpub. The license fee for operation of a brewpub for one calendar year or any part thereof shall as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges. No license fee shall be refunded.
(6) Winery. The license fee for operation of a winery for one calendar year or any part thereof shall be as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges. No license fee shall be refunded.
(Code 1969, § 3-43; Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03; Ord. No. 7-2013, § 2, 9-9-13; Ord. No. 7-2017, §§ 7—12, 12-11-17; Ord. No. 7-2019, § 2(Exh. A), 12-9-19)
294:
Any wholesale dealer in malt beverages and/or wines licensed by the state, or the agent of such wholesale dealer, shall be granted a license to distribute such malt beverages and/or wines in the city upon application for a license to the clerk of the city, the payment of the fee provided for in this article, and the presentation of evidence that he understands the provisions and conditions under which retail licenses are issued.
(Code 1969, § 3-45; Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03)
295:
The application, qualifications and procedures governing the issuance of a retail package malt beverages and/or wine license shall be in accordance with the requirements contained in article II of this chapter. Further, all regulations controlling the sale of malt beverages and/or wine or in any other way pertaining to the sale of beer as contained in sections 6-131 and 6-132 shall have full application to the sale of malt beverages and/or wine as if fully set out as a separate section in this division. It is the intention of this section that malt beverages and/or wine shall be sold only at a qualified malt beverage and/or wine outlet under the application procedures, license qualifications and all other rules and regulations set forth in article II of this chapter, and any further restrictions contained in this article. Nothing contained in this article shall prevent a person from applying for a retail malt beverage and/or wine license and a retail malt beverage and/or wine package license, simultaneously.
(Code 1969, § 3-44; Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03)
296:
The application shall state that it is for a retail consumption dealer's malt beverages and/or wine license and shall be made on forms furnished by the governing authority. The fee for this consumption license shall be as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges as an annual fee for the operation of each calendar year, or any portion of a calendar year.
(Code 1969, § 3-51; Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03; Ord. No. 7-2019, § 2(Exh. A), 12-9-19)
297:
No retail consumption dealers' malt beverages and/or wine license shall be issued to any person unless the business or proposed business to be licensed pursuant to this division is a bona fide eating establishment. For purposes of this section, a "bona fide eating establishment" shall mean any public place selling prepared food for consumption by the public on the premises and deriving at least 50 percent of its total annual gross sales from the sale of prepared meals or foods, in addition to the requirements set forth in section 6-102.
(Code 1969, § 3-52; Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03; Ord. No. 15,2004, § 2, 10-11-04)
298:
Each applicant for a retail consumption dealer's license shall attach to the application evidence of ownership of the building or proposed building or a copy of the lease if the applicant is leasing the building. If the applicant is a franchisee, then such applicant shall attach a copy of the franchise agreement or contract with the application. All premises for which a retail consumption dealer's license shall be issued shall afford therein adequate sanitary toilet facilities and shall be adequately illuminated so that all hallways, passageways and open areas may be clearly seen by the customers therein.
(Code 1969, § 3-53)
299:
No retail consumption dealer's license issued pursuant to this division shall be transferable or assignable to any other person or location, and if a licensed business is sold or closed, it shall be the duty of the licensee to immediately surrender the license to the governing authority. A separate retail consumption dealer's license shall be required for each place of business.
(Code 1969, § 3-55)
300:
All terms, provisions and conditions contained in article II of this chapter, and this article regulating malt beverages and/or wine including, but not limited to, sale restrictions, hours of operation, revocation of licenses and any and all other provisions shall likewise apply to the on-premises consumption of malt beverages and/or wine, as though fully set forth in this article.
(Code 1969, § 3-56; Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03)
301:
If the city commission revokes, suspends or fails to renew any license which has been issued by the commission under this article, the city commission may, notwithstanding the other provisions in this article, review such revocation, suspension or failure to renew and may reinstate such license, subject to all of the following conditions:
(1) Such review cannot be held until at least one year after the date of the revocation, suspension or failure to renew.
(2) The original licensee against whom the revocation, suspension or failure to renew action was taken must make application in writing for reinstatement of his license after the lapse of the one-year period.
(3) The original licensee must have remained in the same business, except for the selling of alcoholic beverages, at the same location continuously since such revocation, suspension or failure to renew.
(4) The original licensee must, at the time of the review, be qualified in all respects for the same type of license originally issued to him, except for those provisions in section 6-61 concerning violations relating to the sale of alcoholic beverages, if the revocation, suspension or failure to renew was a result of such violation.
(5) The application for reinstatement shall be made in accordance with and subject to all of the same provisions, conditions and qualifications as required by this division for the approval of an initial license.
(Code 1969, § 3-49; Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03)
302:
Any person who has previously been granted a malt beverage and/or wine license pursuant to the provisions of this article, may likewise apply, or in the case of an initial application or renewal, designate that the license shall include the grant of a separate license fee for the on-premises consumption of malt beverages and/or wine within the corporate limits of the city. All terms, conditions and provisions of article II of this chapter, apply to a separate license granted for the on-premises consumption of malt beverages and/or wine under the provisions of this article.
(Code 1969, § 3-50; Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03)
303:
Nothing in this article shall preclude a licensee from conducting a malt beverage and/or wine tasting, provided that the licensee complies with all regulations of the state revenue commissioner then in force relative to such malt beverage and/or wine tastings. A copy of any permit issued by the state revenue commissioner authorizing a malt beverage and/or wine tasting in the city shall be filed with the city clerk prior to conducting the malt beverage and/or wine tasting.
(Code 1969, § 3-48; Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03)
304:
In addition to the regulations set forth in article II of this chapter, which shall apply to all malt beverage and/or wine licenses granted pursuant to this article, the following regulations shall also apply to the sale of malt beverages and/or wine within the city:
(1) No screen, partition or other obstruction which prevents a clear view into the interior of a retail outlet from the street, nor any booth within, shall be permitted.
(2) Each retail outlet shall post at least four copies of its complete price list for malt beverages and/or wines, or in lieu thereof, place a price on each bottle for sale.
(3) The state laws and regulations relating to the sale and distribution of malt beverages and/or wine, as revised or hereafter promulgated by the state revenue department, are hereby incorporated into and made a part of this article as if fully set out in this article.
(4) The licensee shall make an immediate report to, and receive approval from, the city commission of any change in the interest in, or ownership of, a malt beverages and/or wine outlet or malt beverages and/or wine business and/or any change in the information as stated in the original application for a license.
(Code 1969, § 3-46; Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03)
305:
Brewer's licenses are authorized in the city; provided, however, that no individual shall be permitted to own or operate a brewery without first obtaining a proper brewer's license from the city in the manner provided in this chapter, and each holder of a brewer's license shall comply with the provisions of this chapter and all applicable state statutes, including rules and regulations promulgated by the department of revenue.
(Ord. No. 7-2017, § 13, 12-11-17)
307:
As a limited exception to the provisions of this chapter which implement and enforce the three-tier system for the manufacture, distribution, and sale of malt beverages established under state law, a brewer's license authorizes the holder of such license to sell directly to the public on its licensed premises up to 3,000 barrels of malt beverages manufactured on such licensed premises per year for: (1) consumption on the premises; and (2) consumption off the premises (sales by the package), provided that such sales by the package shall not exceed a maximum of 288 ounces per consumer per day. Such retail sales are permitted on the days and at the times that the retail sale of malt beverages for consumption on the premises or by the package, as applicable, is authorized for other retailer licensees under this chapter. Under no circumstances shall such malt beverages be sold by a licensed brewer to a licensed retailer or retail consumption dealer for the purpose of resale. Any brewer engaging in the retail sales of malt beverages pursuant to this section shall remit all state and local excise taxes to the proper tax collecting authority. For the purposes of this article, "barrel" means 31 gallons of malt beverages.
(Ord. No. 7-2017, § 15, 12-11-17)
308:
A farm winery may sell its wine and the wine of any other state farm winery licensee at retail in a tasting room or other facility on the premises of the winery for consumption on the premises and in closed packages for consumption off the premises and to sell its wine and the wine of any other state farm winery licensee at retail for consumption on the premises and in closed packages for consumption off the premises in tasting rooms at a location within the city that is one of the five additional locations in the state authorized by O.C.G.A. § 2-6-21.1(b), but only if the annual production of wine by the farm winery is made in state in accordance with the source of berries, fruits or grapes as provided by the laws of the state and the rules and regulations of the state department of agriculture.
(Ord. No. 7-2017, § 16, 12-11-17)
309:
The alcoholic beverage licenses which may be issued to farm wineries under this chapter are:
(1) Wholesaler of farm winery production. A farm winery shall be granted a wholesale license for sale and distribution as provided by O.C.G.A. § 2-6-21.1. Such license shall be issued upon application and payment of established fees and upon presentation of a receipt for payment of the state annual license tax as provided by the referenced code provisions in this section.
(2) Retail package sales of wine. Each retail package sales license shall require that all sales shall be by and through the farm winery tasting room at the site for which said license is issued.
(3) Retail sales of wine. Each license for retail sales of wine and malt beverages for consumption on the premises shall require that all consumption shall be at the farm winery site for which said license is issued. This site shall include any wedding or dining facilities associated with the farm winery.
(4) Multiple farms winery licenses. A farm winery may apply for and, if approved, may be issued multiple farm winery licenses. At the primary farm winery facility where the wine is produced, such site may be licensed for wholesale, package retail sales and on-premises consumption. For any site other than the primary farm winery facility where the wine is produced, up to the maximum number of such sites as may be permitted by state statute, such site may be licensed for package retail sales and on-premises consumption. The license created in accordance with this article shall be limited to farm winery tasting rooms licensed by the state in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 2-6-21.1 et seq., and the licensee shall be permitted to perform only acts allowed in accordance with such statues. No license is hereby created authorized any other use.
(5) Alternate provision. The first license at any site shall have a cost equal to the cost of a city alcoholic beverage license at the time of the application. Any license for two or more categories of sale shall require payment of the additional license fees as provided in the city fee schedule.
(6) Ratio of sales. There shall be no specified or required ratio of alcohol sales to any other income for winery operations. Farm wineries shall operate on such days and hours as are provided by the Georgia Farm Winery Act., O.C.G.A. § 2-6-21.1 et seq., as amended from time to time and by the terms of this section for sale by consumption on the premises.
(7) Premises consumption.
a. A farm winery may apply for a license for on-premises consumption of distilled spirits under the terms as provided under this chapter.
b. A farm winery may apply for a license for on-premises consumption of wine and malt beverages (not produced under the Georgia Farm Winery Act O.C.G.A. § 2-6-21.1 et seq.) under the terms as provided under this chapter.
(Ord. No. 7-2017, § 17, 12-11-17)
310:
(a) A retail cigar shop as specifically defined in this Code, may be issued an on-premises consumption license for sales of beer, malt beverages, wine, and/or distilled spirits, without meeting the food gross sales requirement derived from the sale of prepared meals or food, provided that at least 51 percent of its gross annual sales be derived from the sale of full-sized, hand-rolled cigars, pipe tobaccos, briar wood pipes, humidors, lighters, cutters, and expressly excluding from the calculation of gross annual sales the sale of cigarettes and any and all other tobacco products or smoking paraphernalia not specified in the gross sales requirement. The financial officer or his/her designee shall review the gross income figures from each such establishment, which shall provide such information at the end of the third quarter of each calendar year and at any other time as requested by the director of finance or his/her designee. The financial officer or his/her designee shall determine if the annual sales meet the required ratio and make appropriate recommendations to the city commission.
(b) Any retail cigar shop licensed by and operating within the city shall conduct such business in compliance with the requirements of the Georgia Smokefree Air Act, O.C.G.A. § 31-12-A-1 et seq., the provisions of which are explicitly incorporated herein and made a part hereof by reference.
(Ord. No. 4-2019, § 2, 9-9-19)
311:
(a) Any business located in the C-1 or C-2 zoning districts, which is required to pay a business occupation tax to the City of Cedartown and which does not otherwise meet the requirements for the issuance of a consumption on premises license for malt beverages and wine may obtain such a license, providing that the following conditions are met:
(1) The sale of alcoholic beverages shall be clearly incidental to the primary business conducted on the premises.
(2) Consumption on the premises licensees shall maintain at least 51 percent of their business volume from the sale of merchandise or services, not including alcoholic beverages. The 51 percent ratio shall be determined on a calendar quarter basis on the monthly report submitted by each licensee.
(3) Monthly reports for the preceding month's alcohol and retail or services sales shall be submitted on forms provided by the City of Cedartown, Georgia on or before the 20th day of the month.
(4) To qualify for a license, a retail or business establishment must be open to the public for business a minimum of 32 hours per week.
(Ord. No. 3-2021, § 1, 6-14-21)
315: The books and records of all wholesalers selling or delivering any wine and/or malt beverages to retailers made subject to the taxes levied in this article and the books and records of all retailers made subject to the taxes levied in this article shall be open for inspection and audit by the agents of the city, to ensure compliance with this article, and it shall be unlawful for any person to deny any authorized agent of the city reasonable access to such books and records. Such books and records shall, for wholesalers, contain information showing deliveries of any of such beverages to persons upon whom the tax hereby assessed and levied is imposed separately, and the monthly reports of such wholesalers shall show deliveries made to each retailer, separately, so that sales of any of the beverages described in this section may be identified with respect to each retailer upon whom the tax is imposed by this section.

State Law reference— Imposition of excise tax on malt beverages, O.C.G.A. § 3-5-80.
318:
There is hereby imposed upon and levied against every licensed wholesale dealer in malt beverages an excise tax, in addition to the excise taxes presently levied by the state as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges.
(Ord. No. 7-2019, § 2(Exh. A), 12-9-19)
319: The excise tax levied in this division and imposed upon licensed wholesalers is levied and imposed with respect to malt beverages sold or distributed by such wholesalers in the city to retailers doing business in the city. The excise tax provided for in this division shall be paid by such licensed wholesale dealers to the city on or before the tenth day of the month following the calendar month in which the beverages are sold or disposed of by such licensed wholesale dealer. Every licensee responsible for the payment of the excise tax imposed by this section shall file a monthly report itemizing for the preceding calendar month the exact quantities of malt beverages, by size and type of container, for the month. Each wholesale licensee shall report and remit to the city, on the tenth of the month next succeeding the calendar month in which such beer and malt beverages are sold or disposed of, the tax imposed by this division.
321:
Footnote 5:
State Law reference— Authorization to levy tax on wine, O.C.G.A. § 3-6-60.
322:
(a) In addition to the annual retail wine license fee required, there is hereby levied an excise tax computed at the rate as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges, per liter of wine, which shall be paid to the city on all wine sold, displayed or stored in the city. The per liter tax shall be prorated and a proportionate tax is hereby imposed at like rates on all fractional parts of a liter.
(b) The tax shall be paid to the city by the wholesale distributor on all wines sold to retailers in the city as follows: Each wholesale distributor selling, shipping or in any way delivering wine to any such retailer shall collect the excise tax at the time of delivery and shall remit the same, together with a summary of all deliveries, to each retailer on or before the tenth day of the month following.
(c) Each wholesale distributor shall furnish to the city a summary of all purchase invoices for wine sold to each retailer in the city on or before the tenth of each month following such purchases. Said invoices shall show the amount of excise tax paid.
(d) The city shall have the right to audit, and to require production of records from, each wholesaler supplying retailers in the city and each retailer so supplied.
(e) It shall be unlawful and a violation of this article for any wholesaler to sell, ship or deliver in any manner, any wine to a retail dealer without collecting such tax. It shall be unlawful and a violation of this chapter for any retail dealer to possess, own, hold, store, display or sell any wine on which such tax has not been paid.
(Code 1969, § 3-47; Ord. No. 7-2019, § 2(Exh. A), 12-9-19)
323:
There is hereby levied an excise tax computed at the rate per liter as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges, which shall be paid to the governing authority on all wine sold by the drink within the corporate limits of the city. Such tax shall be paid to the governing authority by the wholesaler on all wine sold to wine retail consumption dealers in the city, as follows: Each wholesaler selling, shipping or in any way delivering wine to any wine retail consumption dealer shall collect the excise tax at the time of delivery to each retail dealer on or before the 15th day of the month following. The tax per liter shall be prorated so that all containers of wine shall be taxed on the basis of per liter rate as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges. It shall be unlawful and a violation of this section for any wholesaler to sell, ship or deliver in any manner any wine to a retail consumption dealer without collecting such tax. It shall be unlawful and a violation of this section for any wine retail consumption dealer to possess, own, hold, store, display or sell any wine on which such tax has not been paid.
(Code 1969, § 3-54; Ord. No. 7-2019, § 2(Exh. A), 12-9-19)
326:
The following classifications of licenses shall be issued pursuant to this article:
(a) Distilled spirits—Package sales.
(b) Distilled spirits—By the drink for consumption on the premises.
No person shall engage in the sale of distilled spirits in the city without first complying with the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03)
327:
Notwithstanding anything in this article to the contrary, the distribution, sale, handling, and other dealing in or possession of distilled spirits in the city is a privilege and not a right, and the issuance of a license under this article shall not create any property rights in the license holder. Furthermore, such privilege shall not be exercised in the city except as licensed under the terms of this article.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03)
328:
The state regulations regarding the distribution of distilled spirits as promulgated and revised by the state revenue department, together with the provisions of O.C.G.A. Title 3, are hereby incorporated into and made a part of this article as if set forth in full herein.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03)
329:
(a) Application for a distilled spirits license under this article shall be made on forms furnished by the city, signed by the applicant under oath, and, at a minimum, shall contain the following information:
(1) The name, age, address, and length of residency of the applicant.
(2) The name, location, and description of the premises or place of business which is to be operated under such a license.
(3) A statement of whether the applicant or, if the applicant is a partnership, corporation, LLC, or other legal entity, any officer or other person with an interest in the application, has made application at any previous time with the city or any other governing authority for any alcoholic beverage license, and, if so, the disposition of such application.
(4) Whether the applicant or, if the applicant is a partnership, corporation, LLC, or other legal entity, any officer or other person with an interest in the application has ever been convicted of a crime other than traffic violations.
(5) Whether any previous alcoholic beverage license issued to the applicant, or if the applicant is a partnership, corporation, LLC, or other legal entity, any officer of other person with an interest in the application, has been revoked by any federal, state, or local government authority, together with a statement of the reasons for such revocation.
(6) A complete listing of any persons or entities who are to be interested directly or indirectly in the profits or losses, or both, of the proposed business.
(7) As to the applicant's proposed manager and employees at the business location, the same information required of the applicant under subsections (1), (3), (4), and (5) of this section.
(8) Name and address of the owner or landlord or resident manager of the property proposed for said license, and a copy of the deed evidencing ownership of the property.
(9) If the applicant is a partnership, corporation, LLC, or other legal entity, a copy of the partnership agreement, articles of incorporation, bylaws, operating agreement, or other agreements or documents reflecting the creation, organization, and/or operation of the entity, together with a certificate of good standing from the Georgia Secretary of State.
(10) Such other information as may be required by the city commission, chief of police, city manager, city attorney, city clerk, building inspector, fire chief, or other city official.
(b) All new applications for distilled spirits licenses under this article shall be accompanied by a nonrefundable investigation fee, paid in cash or certified funds, to defray the city's administrative costs in reviewing and processing said applications as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges.
(c) All new applications for distilled spirits licenses under this article shall also be accompanied by the proper amount of the license fee, paid in cash or certified funds, as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges. In the event the license is denied, refused, or otherwise not issued, such fee shall be returned to the applicant within 15 days of the city's decision on the application.
(d) The making of any untrue or misleading statement in the application for a distilled spirits license under this article shall be sufficient cause for the refusal, suspension, revocation, or cancellation of such license pursuant to the notice and hearing provisions provided in section 6-312 herein.
(e) The application shall also be accompanied by a current certificate from a registered surveyor containing the following information:
(1) A scale drawing of the building or proposed building as situated on the proposed lot;
(2) Proposed off-street parking facilities available to the building;
(3) Both the straight line distance and measured distance in linear feet from areas listed as "prohibited locations" in section 6-131 of this chapter, and, in the case of package sales, any other business or location with a package license;
(4) The requirement of showing these distances shall not exist where the proposed location is more than 650 feet from the "prohibited locations" listed in subparagraph (3), or, in the case of package sales, more than 8,000 feet, as measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground, from another location with a package license, but the surveyor's plat or certificate shall so indicate; and
(5) The current zoning classification for the proposed location.
(f) Applications for package sales shall also be accompanied by a publisher's affidavit evidencing compliance with O.C.G.A. § 3-4-27.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03; Ord. No. 7-2019, § 2(Exh. A), 12-9-19; Ord. No. 3-2025, § 4, 3-10-25)
330:
(a) Each applicant and employee thereof shall furnish a complete set of fingerprints which the city shall forward to the Georgia Bureau of Investigation, who shall search the files of the Georgia Crime Information Center for a period of ten years immediately preceding the date of such application for any evidence of criminal activity. The Georgia Bureau of Investigation shall also submit fingerprints to the Federal Bureau of Investigation under rules established by the Department of Justice for processing and identification of records. If the applicant is a corporation, LLC, partnership, or other legal entity, then all partners, officers, and/or any other principals, managers, and employees of the entity shall be subject to this fingerprinting requirement.
(b) In addition to the bond requirements of O.C.G.A. § 3-4-22, applicants must post with the city a personal performance bond along with their application, said bond to be conditioned upon the faithful observance and performance by the licensee of the rules and regulations contained in this article. Furthermore, said bond shall be payable to the city, in the amount of $10,000.00, and shall be approved and executed in the form specified by the city. Upon the violation of this article or any part thereof, or on the suspension, revocation, fine or other adverse action taken against the license, the city shall determine the amount of the bond to be forfeited in accordance with the nature of the violation, depending the amount of any fine that may be imposed, after notice and a hearing, as provided by section 6-312 of this article. The determination by the city to forfeit all or part of such bond may be in addition to any action taken by the city under section 6-312 of this article. Applicants shall have an affirmative duty to notify the bonding company of the potential adverse actions that can be taken against the bond upon a finding that the applicant has violated the provisions of this article. Proof of said bond shall be furnished to the city within 15 days after the commission has issued or renewed a license pursuant to this article.
(c) Nothing herein shall preclude the city from no longer requiring the bond contained in this section whenever any licensee has established sufficient financial responsibility and/or a record of faithful compliance with federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and ordinances over a period of not less than five years from the granting of a license.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03; Ord. No. 10-2003, § 1, 9-15-03)
331:
In addition to the qualifications set forth in section 6-61 regarding alcoholic beverages generally, applicants for a distilled spirits license under this article shall meet the following qualifications:
(a) No license shall be issued pursuant to this article if the applicant is not at least 21 years of age.
(b) Notwithstanding the provisions of [subsection] 6-61(6) of this chapter, no license shall be issued for package sales pursuant to this article if the applicant or the resident manager of the business location has not been a bona fide resident of Polk County for at least 12 months immediately preceding the date of application and the requirements of O.C.G.A. § 3-4-23 have been met.
(c) No license shall be issued pursuant to this article to any city employee, official, agent, or other representative who has any interest, directly or indirectly in the proposed business.
(d) No more than two retail dealer licenses shall be issued to any one person in the city, and no person or legal entity who holds or has a beneficial interest in two retail dealer licenses in any other county or municipality in the state shall be eligible to receive a retail dealer's license. The terms "person" and "beneficial interest" shall have the same meaning as used in O.C.G.A. Section 3-4-21.
(e) A separate license shall be issued for each premises or business location.
(f) No license shall be issued if the proposed business is in a "prohibited location" as defined in section 6-131 of this chapter, or, in the case of package sales, within 1.25 miles, as measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground, of another location for which a package sale license has been issued pursuant to this article.
(g) Package sales licenses shall only be issued for locations in C-2 zoning districts. Sales by the drink for consumption on the premises licenses shall only be issued for locations in C-1 and C-2 zoning districts. The zoning classification shall be determined at the time of application.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03; Ord. No. 3-2025, § 3, 3-10-25)
332:
(a) The considerations and guidelines for granting or denying a license pursuant to this article shall be the same as for alcoholic beverages generally, as set forth in section 6-64 of this chapter.
(b) In addition to the considerations and guidelines set forth in section 6-64 of this chapter, the city shall also consider the zoning classification for the proposed location and, in the case of package sales, whether said location is a measured distance of 1.25 miles, as measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground, from another premises that holds a package sales license issued pursuant to this article.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03; Ord. No. 3-2025, § 5, 3-10-25)
333:
(a) Within 15 days from the time an application is submitted to the city, the clerk shall notify the chief of police of the application. The chief of police shall investigate the character and criminal record, if any, of the applicant and all identified managers, employees, agents, and/or other interested parties and make a report to the city commission. The clerk shall also refer the application to the building inspector, who shall inspect the proposed licensed premises and likewise issue a report to the city commission. After the police chief and building inspector have rendered their reports, the clerk shall place the matter on the agenda for the next regularly scheduled city commission meeting at which the applicant shall be afforded a hearing. At this meeting, the full city commission may approve or deny the application. The commission may also table the application for further study and investigation or may approve the application with certain conditions that must be met before the license can be issued.
(b) If an application is denied, then the applicant shall be notified in writing of the commission's decision, and the reasons therefore, within ten days. Applicant shall then have 30 days to either request reconsideration of the commission's denial or appeal the commission's decision to the Superior Court of Polk County.
(c) If an application is denied, then the applicant may not submit another application for the same proposed business premises for a period of 12 months from the commission's decision.
(d) If the commission determines that the applicant meets the standards and guidelines for licenses as set forth in this chapter and the applicant has paid the required license and investigation fees, the commission shall issue the license requested.
(e) Upon approval of an application for a license pursuant to this article, the applicant shall have 15 days within which to pay the required license fee. Failure to pay said fee will result in revocation and/or forfeiture of the license previously issued, as well as all rights, duties, and obligations pursuant to this article, and the applicant must reapply for the license.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03; Ord. No. 10-2003, § 2, 9-15-03)
334:
(a) A distilled spirits license issued pursuant to this article shall be valid only for the calendar year indicated thereon, and no such license may be renewed except upon approval of the city commission and payment of the required license fee.
(b) A licensee who desires to continue in business during the subsequent calendar year must make a new application for renewal of his current license prior to November 15 of the year in which the current license expires and pay the required license fee in full, in cash or certified funds, on or before December 31 of that year.
(c) Upon receipt of an application for renewal of an existing license issued pursuant to this article, the clerk shall forward same to the chief of police, who shall then provide a report on any criminal activity of the licensee, his employees, agents, or other representatives, or at the location of the licensed premises during the year.
(d) In considering an application for renewal of an existing license issued pursuant to this article, the commission shall be guided by the considerations and guidelines set forth in section 6-306 and of section 6-64. The commission may take the same action regarding renewal applications that it is empowered to take with regard to an initial application, as set forth in section 6-307 of this article.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03)
335:
The investigation fee for applications submitted pursuant to this article shall be as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges. The annual fee for a license for the package sale of distilled spirits shall be as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges. The approved fee for a license for the sale of distilled spirits by the drink for consumption on the premises shall be as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the approved fee for a license for the sale of distilled spirits by the drink for consumption on the premises in the downtown business district shall be as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges. All fees shall be paid at the time of submission of the application, either in cash or certified funds. Investigative fees shall be nonrefundable and shall be used to defray the city's administrative costs and other expenses in investigating, reviewing, and otherwise processing the application.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03; Ord. No. 7-2013, § 3, 9-9-13; Ord. No. 7-2019, § 2(Exh. A), 12-9-19)
336:
(a) All licenses issued pursuant to this article shall be valid only so long as the licensee is actively engaged in such business, with the exception of holidays, vacations, and periods of renovation, redecoration, or other substantial improvements that would prohibit the operation of business. In the event the licensee shall cease to be actively engaged in the business, or the business is not opened to the public for a period of 60 consecutive days, the license shall expire, and the licensee shall immediately return the license to the city.
(b) Similarly, if the applicant for a license has not commenced operation of business on the proposed licensed premises within 120 days of the issuance of the license, then the license shall lapse and become void. In this event, a new application shall be submitted pursuant to section 6-302.
(c) If a license lapses or expires under this code section, the licensee shall not be entitled to a refund or proration of any fees, taxes, or other charges levied pursuant to this article.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03)
337:
(a) The provisions of section 6-76 of this chapter regarding transfers and assignments of licenses shall apply equally to licenses issued pursuant to this article.
(b) Licenses issued pursuant to this article shall not be transferable from one location to another. Any current holder of a license issued pursuant to this article desiring to discontinue business at one location and commence business at some other location must make a complete new application for the new location.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03)
339:
(a) No license shall be issued pursuant to this article unless the building in which the business will be located is complete and detailed plans of said building and outside premises are attached to the application. If the building is to be constructed at a later date, the applicant shall submit proposed plans and specifications and a building permit for a proposed building to be built or renovated along with the application. In either event, the complete or proposed building shall comply with all ordinances of the city and all building codes incorporated therein, as well as all regulations of the state revenue commissioner and the laws of the state. The building shall be subject to final inspection and approval by the building inspector prior to issuance of a license and shall remain open to inspection by any city official at any time the business is open to consumers.
(b) Each building shall contain sufficient lighting so that the building itself and the premises on all sides thereof are readily visible at all times from the street on which the building is located, so as to reveal all the outside premises of said building.
(c) No tinted windows, screens, partitions or other opaque devices that prevent a clear view of the interior of the building from the street, nor any booths or other compartments inside the building, shall be permitted.
(d) Each applicant for a license pursuant to this article shall attach to the application evidence of ownership of the building and/or real estate on which the building or proposed building is to be located. If the applicant is leasing the building, then the applicant shall submit a copy of the lease.
(e) Each license holder shall post in a conspicuous location within the place of business a sign, printed in letters at least two inches high, reading as follows: "Sale of liquor to persons under 21 years of age strictly prohibited."
(f) No drive-in windows shall be permitted at any premises for which a retail dealer's license has been applied for or issued.
(g) All package sale license holders under this article shall comply with the requirements of O.C.G.A. § 3-4-3 regarding exterior signage on the licensed premises.
(h) The parking area for any licensed premises shall be paved with concrete or asphalt and contain sufficient square footage and parking spaces as required by this Code for retail commercial places of business.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03)
340:
Each retail dealer shall conspicuously display no less than two copies of a printed price list of the distilled spirits offered for sale and one copy of the penal sections of this article on the licensed premises. In lieu of a printed price list, the dealer may have the prices placed on the bottles or on the bottom of the shelf where distilled spirits are exhibited for sale.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03)
341:
No holder of a retail dealer license issued pursuant to this article shall sell, offer for sale, display, or keep in stock at the place of business where distilled spirits are offered for sale any other product, good, or other commodity, other than what is permitted by laws of this state and/or regulations of the state department of revenue as they currently exist and as may be amended from time to time in the future.
(1) Wine, if the license holder also holds a valid and current license to sell wine at said place of business.
(2) Malt beverages or beer, if the license holder also holds a valid and current license to sell malt beverages or beer at said place of business.
(3) Tobacco products.
(4) Mixers, or beverages containing no alcohol and commonly used to dilute distilled spirits.
(5) Ice to be sold in sealed containers only and not to be opened on the premises.
(6) Paper, Styrofoam, or plastic cups.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03)
342:
(a) No retail dealer shall sell or deliver any distilled spirits to any person except in the retailer dealer's place of business. A retail dealer shall be permitted to load purchased goods in a customer's vehicle when the sale physically takes place and monies have been exchanged inside the place of business.
(b) "Curb service" type sales and sales to customers in vehicles parked in the parking area of the place of business are prohibited.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03)
343:
(a) No holder of a license issued pursuant to this article, nor any agent, employee, or other representative of the licensee shall engage in any of the following conduct upon the licensed premises:
(1) Knowingly furnish, sell, or cause or permit to be furnished or sold to any minor alcoholic beverages of any kind.
(2) Knowingly allow or require any person under the age of 18 years in his employment to dispense, serve, sell, or take orders for any alcoholic beverages.
(3) Knowingly sell alcoholic beverages to any person while such person is in an intoxicated condition.
(4) Sell alcoholic beverages on the licensed premises on any day or at any time when such sale is prohibited by law.
(5) Permit any disturbance of the peace, obscenity, or any lewd, immoral, or improper entertainment, conduct, or practice on the licensed premises. If any such conduct occurs, the license holder shall immediately report it to the city police department.
(6) Sell or offer for sale any alcoholic beverages by the use of vending machines.
(7) In the case of package sale licenses, permit any customer to open, consume, or have any open containers of any alcoholic beverages in their possession on the licensed premises.
(8) Knowingly permit any gambling, betting, games of chance, punchboards, slot machines, illegal lottery, or other device for the hazarding of any money or other thing of value on the licensed premises.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03)
344:
(a) Any person, including the licensee, who works in a business with a license issued pursuant to this article shall apply to the police department for a distilled spirits employee identification card, which card shall expire on the person's birthday and be renewable on or before that time. The fee for the initial card shall be as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges. The fee for a replacement card shall be as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges. The fee for renewal of such card shall be as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges. In the event that a renewal of such card is late, an additional fee as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges will be assessed for all renewals after the renewal date for each individual. Fees shall be paid at city hall.
(b) While on duty in the licensed premises, every person required to hold an employee identification card under subsection (a) shall have his employee identification card on their person at all times.
(c) Employees of any licensee under the provisions of this article shall make themselves available for photographing, fingerprinting and such other investigation as may be required by the police department, pursuant to section 6-304 hereof.
(d) The police department shall investigate the employee applicants. A distilled spirits employee identification card shall not be issued to any person who has pled guilty to, or has been convicted of a felony within the last five years. The police department shall report any other detrimental information about an applicant that would tend to affect their qualifications or ability to perform the functions of an employee in the licensed premises to the city commission, and may prohibit the issuance of a distilled spirits identification card where the applicant's record indicates such employment would adversely affect the public health, safety, or welfare, or violate the law.
(e) No licensee under the provisions of this article shall hire any person, nor shall any person work or assist in the licensed premises until such person has procured a distilled spirits employee identification card.
(f) The police department may provisionally grant an identification card to an applicant, pending investigation and report. Where the report, when reviewed, is unfavorable as set out in subsection (d), the department may revoke the card and demand its return.
(g) The police department may, after reasonable notice and hearing (unless waived), revoke an identification card and demand its surrender where the employee violates the provisions of this chapter, or otherwise becomes unqualified or unfit to hold said card.
(h) It shall be unlawful for an employee whose card has been revoked, and upon whom demand for surrender of a card has been made, to refuse to so surrender, or to alter, conceal, deface, or destroy the card.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03; Ord. No. 7-2019, § 2(Exh. A), 12-9-19)
345:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to sell, give away, offer for sale, or in any manner disperse or deliver any distilled spirits by the package within the corporate limits of the city between the hours of 12:00 a.m. (midnight) until 12:30 p.m. on each and every Sunday; and from 11:30 p.m. on each and every Sunday until 8:00 a.m. On each and every Monday; and from 12:00 a.m. midnight Christmas until 8:00 a.m. on the day following Christmas of each year.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to sell, give away, offer for sale, or in any manner disburse or deliver any distilled spirits by the drink within the corporate limits of the city between the hours of 1:30 a.m. and 8:00 a.m. each and every Monday through Saturday; and from 1:30 a.m. until 11:00 a.m. on each and every Sunday; and from 11:30 p.m. on each and every Sunday, until 8:00 a.m. on each and every Monday; and from 12:00 a.m. midnight on Christmas Eve until 8:00 a.m. on the day following Christmas each year.
(c) All businesses who hold a license for the sale of distilled spirits for consumption on the premises shall close and have all patrons or customers out of the premises within 30 minutes after the hours of sale specified in this section.
(Ord. No. 2-2012, § 2, 3-12-12; Ord. No. 4-2012, § 2, 4-9-12; Ord. No. 5-2021, § 1, 12-13-21; Ord. No. 3-2025, § 1, 3-10-25)
Editor's note— Ord. No. 2-2012, § 2, adopted Mar. 12, 2012, repealed former § 6-319 and enacted a new section as set out herein. The former section pertained to similar subject matter and derived from Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03; Ord. No. 2-2004, § 4, 2-9-04.
346:
All retail dealers shall sell distilled spirits in the original unbroken package only, and shall sell no package containing less than 50 milliliters.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03)
347:
(a) No holder of a license issued pursuant to this article shall buy or arrange to buy or in any way effect the transfer of any distilled spirits to its business location, except from a licensed wholesaler.
(b) A holder of a package sales license issued pursuant to this article shall keep no inventory or stock of distilled spirits at any place except the licensed place of business and, within the licensed place of business, the storage area for distilled spirits shall be immediately adjacent to the retail area. Furthermore, no licensee hereunder shall enter into any type of arrangements whereby any type of contract, agreement, or other arrangement whereby distilled spirits ordered by said licensee are stored by a licensed wholesaler.
(c) A holder of a license for consumption of distilled spirits by the drink shall purchase distilled spirits only from licensed wholesalers and in sizes of 750 milliliters or larger, unless a particular brand is not packaged in this size, in which case the licensee shall purchase the next largest size available in such brand.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03)
348:
(a) In the C-1 downtown business district as described in this Code, all holders of a license for consumption of distilled spirits by the drink shall maintain at least 40 percent of their annual gross income from the sale of foods. In all other zones, holders of a license for consumption of distilled spirits by the drink shall maintain at least 50 percent of their annual gross income from the sale of foods. If said records indicate that the licensee is not meeting the requirements of this section, then their license may be subject to suspension or revocation under section 6-312 hereof.
(b) Within 120 days after having been issued a license for consumption of distilled spirits by the drink on the premises, the licensee shall submit to the city a statement from a certified public accountant or registered public accountant that the income requirements set forth in this section have been met for the first 90 days after the applicant received his license. Thereafter, on a quarterly basis and at each and every time of the license renewal, or upon request of the city, each license holder shall submit to the city a statement from a certified or registered public accountant verifying that the income requirements as set forth in this section have been met.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 2, 8-11-03; Ord. No. 8,2010, § 4, 6-14-10)
349:
(a) In addition to the annual license fees imposed and required by this article, there is hereby levied and imposed an excise tax on all package sales of distilled spirits as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Abandoned animal means an animal that is unattended and uncared for and is:
(1) Placed on public property or within a public building.
(2) Placed on private property or within a private building without the consent of the private property's owner, custodian or tenant.
(3) On or within the property of the animal's owner or custodian and has remained unattended and uncared for in excess of 36 hours.
Animal means any living nonhuman species of animal, domestic or wild.
At large means off the premises of the owner and not under the control of the owner, a member of his immediate family or some other person, either by leash, cord, chain or some other holding device.
Control means that an animal is under the control of its owner if it is on his private property. If the animal is off the owner's property, control is defined in section 14-6.
Dangerous animal means any wild mammal, reptile or fowl which is not naturally tame or gentle but is of a wild nature or disposition and which, because of its size, vicious propensity or other characteristics, would constitute a danger to human life or property if not kept or maintained in a safe manner or in secure quarters; and any domestic mammal, reptile or fowl which, because of its size, vicious propensity or other characteristic, would constitute a danger to human life or property if not kept or maintained in a safe manner or in secure quarters.
Dangerous dog means any dog that, according to the records of an appropriate authority:
(1) Inflicts a severe injury on a human being without provocation on public or private property.
(2) Aggressively bites, attacks or endangers the safety of human beings without provocation after the dog has been classified as a potentially dangerous dog and after the owner has been notified of such classification.
Owner means any natural person or any legal entity, including, but not limited to, a corporation, partnership, firm or trust owning, possessing, harboring, keeping or having custody or control of a dog, dangerous dog or a potentially dangerous dog within this city.
Potentially dangerous dog means any dog that at any time and without [provocation] bites, injures, or behaves in an aggressive manner toward a human being that would cause a reasonable person to be in fear of imminent injury or bodily harm from the dog.
Poundkeeper means any person engaged by the city to maintain facilities for impounding animals under this chapter and otherwise carrying out the provisions of this chapter.
Proper enclosure means an enclosure for keeping a dangerous or potentially dangerous animal securely confined indoors on the owner's property. If the animal is not kept indoors, a proper enclosure shall be a securely enclosed and locked fence, pen or other structure suitable for both preventing the animal's escape and small children's entry. Such a structure shall have secure sides and a secure top and provide the animal protection from the elements. If the animal is confined within a fence, all sides of the fence shall be high enough to prevent the animal from escaping over it, and the bottom of the fence shall be constructed so as to prevent the animal from escaping underneath it.
Records of an appropriate authority means records of any state, county or municipal law enforcement agency; records of any county or municipal animal control agency; records of any county board of health; records of any federal, state or local court; or records of a dog control officer provided for in this article.
Severe injury means any physical injury that results in broken bones or disfiguring lacerations requiring multiple sutures or cosmetic surgery or a physical injury that results in death.
Stray means an animal running at large in the city without a proper license as provided for in this chapter.

(a) Upon receiving a report of a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog within a dog control officer's jurisdiction from a law enforcement agency, animal control agency, rabies control officer or county board of health, the dog control officer shall make such investigations and inquiries with regard to such report as may be necessary to carry out the provisions of this chapter.

(Code 1969, § 4-6.1)
427:
(a) As applied to the owners of potentially dangerous dogs, the procedures provided for in this section must be carried out as a necessary condition for the enforcement of the provisions of this chapter against such owners. As applied to the owners of dangerous dogs, the procedures provided for in this section shall not be an essential element of any crime provided for in this chapter.
(b) When a dangerous dog or a potentially dangerous dog is classified as such, the dog control officer shall notify the dog's owner of such classification.
(c) The notice to the owner shall meet the following requirements:
(1) The notice shall be in writing and mailed by certified mail to the owner's last known address or hand delivered to the owner by the animal control officer or a city police officer.
(2) The notice shall include a summary of the dog control officer's findings that formed the basis for the dog's classification as a dangerous or potentially dangerous dog.
(3) The notice shall be dated and shall state that the owner, within 15 days after the date shown on the notice, has a right to request a hearing on the dog control officer's determination that the dog is a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog.
(4) The notice shall state that the hearing, if requested, shall be before the municipal court.
(5) The notice shall state that if a hearing is not requested, the dog control officer's determination that the dog is a dangerous dog or a potentially dangerous dog will become effective for all purposes under this chapter on a date specified in the notice, which shall be after the last day on which the owner has a right to request a hearing.
(6) The notice shall include a form to request a hearing before the municipal court and shall provide specific instructions on mailing or delivering such request to the court.
(d) When the municipal court receives a request for a hearing as provided in subsection (c) of this section, it shall schedule such hearing within 30 days after receiving the request. The court shall notify the dog owner in writing by certified mail of the date, time and place of the hearing, and the notice shall be mailed to the dog owner at least ten days prior to the date of the hearing. At the hearing, the owner of the dog shall be given the opportunity to testify and present evidence. The court shall also receive such other evidence and hear such other testimony as it may find reasonably necessary to make a determination either to sustain, modify or overrule the dog control officer's classification of the dog.
(e) Within ten days after the date of the hearing, the court shall notify the dog owner in writing by certified mail of its determination on the matter. If such determination is that the dog is a dangerous dog or a potentially dangerous dog, the notice shall specify the date upon which that determination is effective.
(Code 1969, § 4-6.2; Ord. No. 10-1998, § III, 3-9-98)
428:
(a) It is unlawful for an owner to have or possess within this state and the city a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog without a certificate of registration issued in accordance with the provisions of this section. This certificate shall be in addition to any standard dog license and fees or other requirements of this chapter (see section 14-7).
(b) Subject to the additional requirements of subsection (c) of this section for dangerous dogs, the dog control officer shall issue a certificate of registration to the owner of such dog if the owner presents to the dog control officer or the dog control officer otherwise finds sufficient evidence of:
(1) A proper enclosure to confine the dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog; and
(2) The posting of the premises where the dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog is located with a clearly visible sign warning that there is a dangerous dog on the property. This sign shall be as designed by the department of natural resources and shall be posted in a conspicuous place so that it may be seen by the general public.

(1) A policy of insurance in the amount of at least $250,000.00 issued by an insurer authorized to transact business in this state insuring the owner of the dangerous dog against liability for any personal injuries inflicted by the dangerous dog; or
(2) A surety bond in the amount of $250,000.00 or more issued by a surety company authorized to transact business in this state payable to any person injured by the dangerous dog.

(a) Whenever any dog bites a person, the owner of the dog shall immediately notify the poundkeeper who shall order the dog held on the owner's premises or shall have it impounded at the owner's expense for a period of two weeks.
